Authoritarian states: Conditions for emergence
Economic conditions, social division, the impact of war, and weaknesses of the political system. Compare how these conditions created opportunities; do not assume all four mattered equally.
Russia 1917 / Cuba before 1959; Stalin’s party struggle is a distinct phase.
Methods of emergence
Persuasion and coercion; leadership; ideology; the use of force and propaganda. Connect the method to how it changed political power.
Lenin’s Bolshevik organisation; Stalin’s appointments and alliances; Castro’s guerrilla and urban coalition.
Consolidation and maintenance
Legal methods, force, charismatic leadership and propaganda. Explain the relationship between institutions and personal rule.
Constituent Assembly and faction ban; Stalin’s purges and constitution; CDRs and the Cuban Communist Party.
Opposition
Nature, extent and treatment of opposition. Distinguish opposition within the ruling movement from dissent in wider society.
Kronstadt; Left and Right Opposition; Escambray resistance and Cuban exile movements.
Foreign policy and power
The impact of successes and failures in foreign policy on the maintenance of power. Keep linking foreign affairs to domestic authority.
Brest-Litovsk; Stalin and the Second World War; Bay of Pigs, missile crisis and Soviet aid.
Aims and results of domestic policies
Economic, political, cultural and social aims and outcomes. Test success against a stated criterion and time span.
NEP, collectivisation and industrialisation; Cuban agriculture, literacy and health.
Women and minorities
Impact of policies on women and minorities: legal rights, lived experiences, uneven gains and repression.
Soviet family policy and deportations; Cuban gender and racial equality alongside exclusion.
Extent of authoritarian control
Assess both coercion and consent. Explain variations by period, social group and institution.
Avoid equating official claims of total control with uniform obedience.
Cold War: Ideology, fear and aggression; economic interests; comparisons of US and Soviet roles.
Tehran, Yalta, Potsdam, Eastern Europe, Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, Berlin.
Containment, peaceful coexistence, Sino-Soviet relations, Sino-US relations, détente and confrontation.
Korea, Hungary, Berlin, Cuba, Vietnam, border clashes, Nixon in China and SALT.
Ideological challenges and dissent, economic problems, the arms race and the ending of the Cold War.
Reagan, Gorbachev, INF, Eastern Europe, 1989, and the distinction between Cold War end and USSR collapse.
Study the impact of two leaders, each from a different region, on the course and development of the Cold War.
Truman/Stalin; Kennedy/Khrushchev; Reagan/Gorbachev. Identify each leader’s decisions and constraints.
Study the economic, social and cultural impact of the Cold War on two countries from different regions, excluding the US and USSR.
Cuba (Americas) and Germany (Europe); distinguish East and West Germany rather than treating their experiences as identical.
Study causes, impact and significance of two Cold War crises from different regions.
Berlin (Europe) and Cuba (Americas), supported by Korean and other examples. Avoid two European crises when two regions are required.
